Adding a few technical clarifications from engineering side:

- KMS: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) bound to the customer account/ARN. Keys and encrypted snapshots stay in-region. If you require HSM-backed keys, we can discuss an enterprise add-on with dedicated HSMs in certain regions.

- VPC connectivity: Redwood Private supports three connectivity patterns:
  * AWS PrivateLink (recommended) — minimal routing changes, keeps traffic on AWS backbone, supports endpoint policies.
  * VPC Peering — direct routing, requires route table entries on both sides; best for lower-latency workloads.
  * Site-to-site VPN — for on-prem connections; can be used with or without NAT.

- Logs & retention: We can export CloudTrail + application access logs to an S3 bucket in your account and region. Retention and lifecycle policies are customer-controlled; Redwood can push logs but we do not retain customer audit logs beyond configured retention without explicit agreement.

- Backups & snapshots: Encrypted snapshots are retained in the same region by default; cross-region replication only happens if specifically enabled by the customer.

If you'd like, I can provide a one-page diagram for each connectivity pattern (I will produce a PrivateLink VPC flow diagram).

- Priyom
